subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core meeting-lifecycle primitive now, and if so what storage, authorization, transcript, and handoff-layer shape should it use?
rationale: The requested capability is plausible and already scoped by discussion, but accepting it would add new core CLI/API, persistent state, transcript, and cross-agent security behavior that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core lifecycle
options.body: Accept the direction as a core feature, require SQLite or an explicitly named artifact owner, define transcript/privacy and authorization rules, and ask for a focused implementation PR.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API work first
options.body: Keep this issue open but require plugin SDK or handoff primitives to mature before adding core meeting verbs.

options.title: Do not pursue core meetings
options.body: Close the core direction and route future experiments to plugins or ClawHub unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept the direction as a core feature, require SQLite or an explicitly named artifact owner, define transcript/privacy and authorization rules, and ask for a focused implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the strongest visible scoping review on this issue and has adjacent history in the sessions/A2A surfaces.
